page: Google Cloud Platform ct6e-standard-4t is an accelerator-optimized machine belonging to the TPU Machines family. It integrates dedicated host compute resources with specialized machine learning hardware, featuring 180 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 720 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

Hardware acceleration is driven by four Google TPU v6e chips, providing an aggregate of 128 GB of accelerator memory across the quartet. This makes the architecture tailored for high-throughput tensor computations. The instance includes no local storage volumes, necessitating network-attached block storage or object storage for operational file systems and model artifacts. It also provisions zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses by default.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, bundling four TPU v6e accelerators with 180 dedicated host cores provides high compute density for machine learning workflows compared to managing fragmented smaller instances. Workloads best aligned with the ct6e-standard-4t include distributed deep learning training, large language model inference, computer vision training, and high-performance tensor-based mathematical modeling.
